entry.title: COP31 Nears Close as ‘Weak’, ‘Compromised’ Draft Draws Fierce Backlash
entry.summary:
ANTALYA, Türkiye, November 19 (IPS) - Civil society organisations and delegates from climate-vulnerable countries have sharply criticised the latest draft of the Presidency-led cover decision at the UN climate summit. They accuse negotiators of removing commitments on fossil fuels and failing to provide concrete climate finance, as the talks enter their final hours.

entry.title: Kenya Contained Ebola With Preparation, Not Luck. Africa Needs More of the Same
entry.summary:
NAIROBI, November 19 (IPS) - Last week, on 11 November, Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient, just 37 days after the country recorded the first-ever case of the virus in its territory. If no new cases emerge over the next six weeks, Kenya will be officially declared Ebola free on 23 December. So far, zero community transmission has been recorded in the country.

entry.title: Protecting Wildlife Requires Gender Equity
entry.summary:
MONTREAL, Canada, November 19 (IPS) - The United States isn’t just lagging behind the global effort to protect biodiversity, it’s pulling in the opposite direction. When the 196 nations that are parties to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity concluded their annual 17th Conference of Parties (COP17) in Yerivan, Armenia, last month, the only member state not there (also the only one that hasn’t ratified the CBD) was the United States. It’s an outlier on both biodiversity and the gender issues related to it.

Read the full story, “Protecting Wildlife Requires Gender Equity”, on globalissues.org →

entry.title: World’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
entry.summary:
The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, delivered its judgment on Thursday in the case of The Gambia v. Myanmar on the application of the Genocide Convention, finding Myanmar responsible for the crime against the country’s ethnic Rohingya, the first such ruling against a State.
